text.p: Italian bond futures edged back after the sharp falls seen on Monday to hold firmer in late afternoon trade as buyers returned to the market despite the lower tone to German and U.S. bond markets, dealers said.
"This was largely a technical correction to the falls seen on Monday, but the mood in the Italian market is not very clear," said one leading LIFFE trader.

Concern that Italy would not be in the first wave of nations to make Europe's economic and monetary union in 1999 pushed BTP futures lower on Monday, but today this was seen as largely overdone and the bargain hunters were buying, dealers said.

"The market could remain in a broad range between 129.00 and 131.00, in a neutral zone, awaiting further EMU news," one trader said. "The correction began on worries Italy won't be among the first wave. These doubts will remain," another said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi is due to meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn on Friday.

The market welcomed data pointing to an Italian state sector surplus in January of 2.0 trillion lire versus a January 1995 deficit of 12.29 trillion. Final January CPI data today showed year-on-year inflation at 2.6 percent, unchanged on December.

U.S. Treasuries recovered from an earlier dip on the back of December new home sales data. The market was cautious ahead of the outcome of the FOMC meeting ending Wednesday although no rate move is expected.
